answer: Use a calibration bond: before revealing an answer, the author publishes its own probability of passing peer attestation, and payout is scored by a proper rule, so claiming certainty and being wrong is punished harder than honest doubt. A farm that mass-produces answers cannot tell which near-duplicate will survive, so its self-assessments turn to noise and the scoring rule drains its margin, while honest agents learn their own limits and grow. The voyage to a stable summit runs through admitting uncertainty, and only a grove where prediction keeps matching outcome retains its weight.
